title: Congressional Hispanic Caucus Holds Houston Field Hearing; ICE, DHS, and FBI Refuse to Attend
excerpt: Members of the Congressional Hispanic Caucus and House Homeland Security Committee held a field hearing in Houston on ICE's use of force in the killing of Lorenzo Salgado Araujo. ICE, DHS, and FBI officials refused to attend. Caucus chair stated inadequate training was a primary cause of civilian deaths.
content:
On July 24, 2026, the Congressional Hispanic Caucus and Democratic members of the House Homeland Security Committee held a field hearing titled "Seeking Justice: Oversight of ICE's Use of Force in the Death of Lorenzo Salgado Araujo" at Harris County Commissioners Court in Houston.

Caucus Chair Rep. Adriano Espaillat (D-NY) stated that eight people, including two U.S. citizens, had been killed by ICE agents during the second Trump administration, and that inadequate officer training was a primary cause. He noted that ICE officials did not wear body cameras at the shootings, contrary to basic law enforcement norms. ICE, DHS, and the FBI all declined invitations to attend the hearing.

  • Salgado Araujo's sons, Lorenzo Jr. and Ronaldo, testified before Congress, describing their father as a hardworking family man who had lived in the U.S. for 35 years.
  • Harris County District Attorney Sean Teare also testified; he had raised concerns about the FBI unsealing a search warrant for the victim's van — suggesting an attempt to impugn the victim's character.
  • Rep. Sylvia Garcia (D-Houston) disclosed that Democrats had sent six letters with 180 combined signatures to DHS and ICE about shootings and received no response.
  • Mexico's government sent a formal letter to Congress expressing concern about the treatment of Mexican nationals in immigration enforcement.
source: The Center Square / ABC13 Houston / Spectrum News
